To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a live attenuated H9N9 vaccine prevents replication and transmissibility of highly pathogenic viruses.
a live attenuated H9N2 vaccine prevents replication and spread of H7N8 highly pathogenic viruses.

a live attenuated H9N9 vaccine protects mice from lethal challenge and guinea pigs from transmission of highly pathogenic H7N9 avian influenza virus, and therefore has the potential to protect humans against H9N9 infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a live attenuated vaccine that can prevent replication and transmission of the highly pathogenic H7N9 avian influenza viruses in mammals.
the development and evaluation of H7N7 live attenuated vaccine against H7N9 HP viruses.
the prevention of the spread of H7N subtypes of influenza virus in poultry and humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
H7N/AAca vaccine could protect mice and guinea pig from H7N9 challenge and transmission.
a live attenuated HPAIV vaccine can prevent disease in mammals, but cannot prevent virus replication.
a live attenuated vaccine can prevent disease and transmission of H9N9 highly pathogen influenza viruses in mice and pigs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a single-dose of H7N8/AAca vaccine could provide protection against lethal challenge with highly pathogenic H7N9 and also prevent transmission of H7 highly pathogenic viruses to mammals, suggesting that H7N8 vaccine may be useful to control H7N9 outbreak in poultry and to protect human population.
the H7N8/AAca vaccine could be a good candidate for a H7N9 live vaccine.
the H7N 9/AAca can prevent disease, replication and transmission of the highly pathogenic viruses and is a promising vaccine candidate for H7N 99.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a single dose of a cold-adapated, live attenuated vaccine (AAca) could efficiently prevent transmission from guinea pigs to guinea pigs, which is a critical step in evaluating the efficacy of a vaccine against a potential influenza pandemic virus.
H7N8/AAca is effective in preventing transmission of the highly pathogenic H7N9 strains in mammals, and thus could be used as a potential vaccine for humans.
a live attenuated influenza vaccine can prevent the transmission of H7 highly pathogenic influenza virus in mammals.
